user.title: Add a eufy account
user.description: Sign in with the eufy account that can see your HomeBase. Home Assistant keeps the signed-in session in a private store, so a restart does not sign in again.

data_description.email: The email address of the eufy account that owns the HomeBase, or of an account the home is shared with.
data_description.password: Used for this sign-in. eufy limits how often an account may sign in, so Home Assistant reuses the stored session afterwards instead of signing in again.
data_description.country: The country your eufy app signs in with (shown on its sign-in screen). eufy lists a device only under the country it was set up or shared under. Empty means Home Assistant's country.

reauth_confirm.title: Enter the eufy password again
reauth_confirm.description: eufy no longer accepts the saved sign-in for {account}: the password was rejected, none is saved, or eufy asks for a two-step verification code. Enter the current password, and Home Assistant signs in to eufy once to check it.

data_description.password: The current password of the eufy account. Repeated failed sign-ins lock the account for 24 hours, so check it before submitting.

reauth_take_over.title: Sign the other client out of eufy?
reauth_take_over.description: Another app, device or integration is signed in with {account}. Continuing signs Home Assistant in to eufy and signs that other client out. Local control of your HomeBase keeps working meanwhile, so you can close this and try again later instead.

reconfigure.title: Sign in to eufy again
reconfigure.description: Home Assistant signs in to eufy once for {account} and keeps the new session. Use this after another app or device signed in with the account, after changing its password, or when the connection to eufy looks stale. Leave the password empty to sign in with the saved one. eufy limits how often an account may sign in, and repeated failed sign-ins lock it for 24 hours, so submit deliberately.

data_description.password: Optional. Leave empty to sign in with the saved password. Enter the account's current password to check it with eufy and save it in place of the old one.

verify_code.title: Enter the eufy verification code
verify_code.description: This eufy account uses two-step verification: eufy accepted the password and asks for the code it sends by e-mail. Enter the code to finish the sign-in. If no e-mail arrives, close this dialog and try again later; each attempt is a sign-in.

data_description.verify_code: The code from eufy's e-mail. Use the newest one if several arrived.

error.invalid_email: That is not an email address. Check it and try again; nothing was sent to eufy.
error.login_challenge: eufy wants a captcha for this sign-in. Sign in once in the eufy app on your phone, then try again here.
error.invalid_verify_code: eufy did not accept the code. Enter the newest code from eufy's e-mail; a new one may be on its way.
error.invalid_auth: eufy rejected the email or password; check both. Repeated failed sign-ins lock the account for 24 hours.
error.login_limited: eufy is temporarily refusing sign-ins for this account. Wait before trying again: each attempt restarts the wait, and repeated attempts can lock the account for 24 hours.
error.session_replaced: Another app, device or integration signed in with this account and eufy ended the earlier session. Close that other client or wait, then try again.
error.session_rejected: eufy accepted the sign-in but then refused the session. Wait a few minutes, then try again.
error.cannot_connect: Home Assistant could not reach eufy. Check the internet connection and try again.

abort.already_configured: This eufy account is already set up in Home Assistant.
abort.reauth_successful: eufy accepted the password. Home Assistant saved it and reloaded the account.
abort.reconfigure_successful: eufy accepted the sign-in. Home Assistant kept the session and reloaded the account.

init.title: eufy Home Security options
init.description: A change reloads the integration, except Sessions per HomeBase and Recording length, which apply at once.

detections.name: Detections and alarm
detections.description: The HomeBase announces a detection but never its end, and normally ends an alarm itself.

data_description.detection_hold: 5–300 s, 10 by default. A detection sensor turns off this long after the detection's own time. A detection that arrives after its hold has run out still fires its event.
data_description.alarm_timeout: 1–60 min, 10 by default. A safety net for an alarm whose end the HomeBase never reports: the panel then leaves Triggered or Pending, shows the guard mode last reported and reads it again.

camera_images.name: Camera images
camera_images.description: What a camera shows for a detection.

data.live_snapshot: Live snapshot for cameras without a detection image

data_description.camera_image: Thumbnail, then HD (default): the event's 640×360 thumbnail in about {thumbnail_seconds} s, then the first frame of its recording in about {hd_seconds} s plus decoding. Thumbnail only: never reads the recording. HD only: the recording's frame alone, so an event without a recording shows no image. Refresh event image follows this choice. None of them wakes a camera; Capture live image always does. After a change, cameras show no image until their next detection or button press.
data_description.live_snapshot: Off by default. A camera with no detection image yet shows one live picture instead, at most every 5 minutes. Wakes a battery camera, which costs battery.

data_description.station_sessions: {min_sessions}–{max_sessions}, {default_sessions} by default. Connections held to each HomeBase: one for detections and the first live view, one for event images, one more per further live view, so {default_live} cameras at once by default. A HomeBase holds about {max_sessions} across all apps and Home Assistant instances and drops one past that, the eufy app's included; give a second instance a small value such as 2. A live view past the limit waits briefly, then is refused. Ends no running live view.
data_description.record_length: 5–300 s, 30 by default. Length of a Record clip when the action names none. Wakes a battery camera for that long.

history.name: Event history
history.description: Images and videos are saved as files under {history_path}, a folder per camera; browse them under Media > My media.

data_description.event_history_days: 0–365, 7 by default. Saves every image a camera or preset shows, named with date, time, camera and what it shows. Older days are deleted; 0 saves nothing. In Home Assistant Container, mount a host directory at /media to keep them across updates.
data_description.event_videos: Off by default. Copies each recording a HomeBase makes from now on into the event history as an MP4, next to its image. Played from the HomeBase's storage, so no camera wakes. Needs Event history above 0 days; videos take far more space than images. Not for a camera without a HomeBase.

eufy_account.name: eufy account
eufy_account.description: Home Assistant reuses its saved eufy session; eufy allows only a few sign-ins per account per day.

data.session_probe: Check the eufy session every 6 hours
data.cloud_push: Cloud push for cameras without a HomeBase

data_description.country: The country your eufy app signs in with (shown on its sign-in screen). eufy lists a device only under the country it was set up or shared under. Empty means Home Assistant's country. A change asks eufy once for the devices, which can cost a sign-in.
data_description.session_probe: On by default. A minute after start and every 6 hours, one device-list read with the saved session, never a sign-in. When another app or device has ended Home Assistant's session, the repair then shows within that time. Off: noticed at the next command that needs eufy or the next restart.
data_description.cloud_push: Off by default. Needed for the detections of a camera without a HomeBase, such as the T8170 Battery SoloCam, which sends them only through eufy's cloud. Home Assistant listens for eufy's push messages like the phone app, which keeps working. HomeBase detections still arrive locally, and one that arrives both ways fires once. The messages pass through eufy's and Google's servers and can arrive late or not at all.

more_countries.name: Extra countries (experimental)
more_countries.description: Experimental and little tested. Each extra country is one more sign-in to the account, on that country's eufy region: it can end Home Assistant's eufy session or the eufy app's, and it spends sign-ins from eufy's small daily limit. Use it only for a shared home that is otherwise missing, and remove it if the account keeps being signed out.

data.scan_regions: Look for devices under every sign-in country on each refresh

data_description.extra_countries: Empty by default. eufy lists a home shared with this account only to a sign-in with the country of the account that shared it. Add that country when it differs from the sign-in country. A change asks eufy once for the devices under every country.
data_description.scan_regions: Off by default. A sign-in country that listed no devices is not asked again. On: every device list asks each of them (Refresh device list, the session check, the hourly refresh for a camera without a HomeBase), so a device added later shows up; asking one whose session has run out signs in to it.

session_replaced.title: eufy ended Home Assistant's session for {account}

confirm.title: Sign Home Assistant in to eufy again
confirm.description: Another app, device or integration signed in with the eufy account {account}, and eufy ended Home Assistant's session; local control of your HomeBase keeps working from the cached account. Home Assistant will sign in to eufy once with the saved password, which signs the other client out. eufy limits how often an account may sign in, so do this only when the other client is no longer needed. To avoid this for good, give Home Assistant its own eufy account, shared from the owner's account.

abort.login_failed: Signing in to eufy failed, so nothing changed and this repair stays open. Wait a while before trying again: repeated failed sign-ins lock the account for 24 hours. You can also sign in again at any time with Reconfigure, on the account's menu under Settings > Devices & services.
abort.entry_not_loaded: The eufy account is not loaded in Home Assistant right now. Use Reconfigure on the account's menu under Settings > Devices & services, which signs in again whether or not the account is loaded, or wait until it has finished loading and open this repair again.

login_limited.title: eufy is refusing sign-ins for {account}
login_limited.description: eufy is refusing sign-ins for the eufy account {account}. The next sign-in is allowed after {time}. Local control of your HomeBase keeps working from the cached account. Do not sign in sooner, in Home Assistant or elsewhere: each early attempt can restart the wait. This notice clears at that time, or when Home Assistant next starts the integration without needing a sign-in.

login_limited_no_wait.title: eufy is refusing sign-ins for {account}
login_limited_no_wait.description: eufy is temporarily refusing sign-ins for the eufy account {account}. Local control of your HomeBase keeps working from the cached account. Wait before signing in again, in Home Assistant or elsewhere: each early attempt can restart the wait. This notice clears when Home Assistant next starts the integration without needing a sign-in.

confirm.title: Allow one more key fetch for {station}
confirm.description: {station} rejects its key, even after Home Assistant fetched the key from eufy again once, so its entities are unavailable; Home Assistant does not fetch the key again by itself. Confirm to reload the eufy account and allow one more key fetch, for example after the station was reset or moved to another account. If it still rejects the key, this repair comes back.

abort.entry_not_loaded: The eufy account or this station is not loaded in Home Assistant right now. Wait until it has finished loading, then open this repair again.
abort.reset_failed: Home Assistant could not allow another key fetch, so nothing changed and this repair stays open. Try again later.

credentials_refreshed.title: Fetched the key for {station} again
credentials_refreshed.description: {station} rejected its old key, so Home Assistant fetched its key or owner id from eufy again. No sign-in was needed. You can dismiss this notice.

credentials_refreshed_login.title: Fetched the key for {station} again, with a sign-in
credentials_refreshed_login.description: {station} rejected its old key, so Home Assistant fetched its key or owner id from eufy again. This cost one eufy sign-in, and eufy limits how often an account may sign in. You can dismiss this notice.

account_id_mismatch.title: {station} stamps its events with another eufy account
account_id_mismatch.description: The HomeBase {station} stamps its records with an owner account other than the one Home Assistant sends with its commands, so it may silently ignore arming, disarming and setting changes. Home Assistant has not changed anything and never adopts another account on its own. Check that this eufy account owns the HomeBase or is a member it serves, then reload the integration; the check runs again after a reload.

media_not_persistent.title: Camera event history is not kept across container updates
media_not_persistent.description: Camera images are saved to {path}, but nothing is mounted there, so they are lost when the Home Assistant container is recreated or updated. Mount a directory of the host at /media, for example `- /srv/homeassistant/media:/media` under `volumes:` in docker-compose.yaml, and recreate the container. To stop saving images instead, set Event history to 0 in the integration's options.

push_not_running.title: eufy cloud push is not running for {account}
push_not_running.description: Cloud push is switched on for the eufy account {account}, but Home Assistant is not receiving eufy's push messages right now. Until it is, detections from cameras without a HomeBase, and changes made in the eufy app, arrive late or not at all. Local control and detections from a HomeBase keep working. Home Assistant keeps retrying by itself, and this notice clears when push runs again. If it stays, check that Home Assistant can reach the internet, and look at the log for the reason. To stop using cloud push, switch it off in the integration's options.

cipher_unavailable.title: eufy has no key for {station}
cipher_unavailable.description: {station} uses key number {cipher} for its local connection, but eufy holds no such key for the station's owner, so Home Assistant cannot connect to it and its entities are unavailable. Signing in again does not help. In the eufy app, on the account that set the station up, check that the station is still there and shared with the account Home Assistant uses; share it again if needed. Then reload the integration: Home Assistant asks eufy again on every reload, and on its own at most once an hour.

key_unusable.title: eufy serves an unusable key for {station}
key_unusable.description: {station} uses an older connection method whose key eufy serves in a form that cannot be read, so Home Assistant cannot connect to it and its entities are unavailable. Fetching the key again returns the same, and signing in again does not help. If the eufy app offers a firmware update for this device, install it, then reload the integration.

no_devices.title: No eufy devices found for {account}
no_devices.description: The eufy account {account} lists no devices ({regions}), so Home Assistant has nothing to set up. Home Assistant does not ask again by itself. Check in the eufy app that the account sees the HomeBase or camera; a shared account sees only what the owner shared with it, and only after it accepted the invitation. Check that the integration's eufy sign-in country (in its options) is the country your eufy app signs in with, and add the country of anyone who shared a home with this account as an extra sign-in country: eufy lists a device only under the country it was set up or shared under. Changing a country asks eufy again. Otherwise turn on Look for devices under every sign-in country on each refresh and press Refresh device list on the eufy account device; you can turn it off again once the devices show.

confirm.title: Look for the shared devices again
confirm.description: The eufy account {account} has an invitation it has not accepted: {invites}. eufy shows a shared home or device only after the invitation is accepted. Accept it in the eufy app, signed in with this account, then confirm here: Home Assistant reloads the eufy account and asks eufy once for its devices. If an invitation is still open, this repair comes back.

abort.entry_not_loaded: The eufy account is not loaded in Home Assistant right now. Wait until it has finished loading, then open this repair again.

auth_failed.message: eufy rejected the saved password for this account, or none is saved. Re-enter it in the reauthentication dialog; Home Assistant will not try the old password again.

guard_mode_not_applied.message: The HomeBase did not apply {target}. The panel shows the mode the HomeBase last reported. If this keeps happening, check in the eufy app that the HomeBase is shared with this eufy account.

setting_not_applied.message: The HomeBase did not apply the change to {target}. The entity shows the value the HomeBase last reported; check that the device is online and try again.

setting_device_unavailable.message: The device {target} belongs to cannot be addressed, so nothing was sent and the entity still shows the value the HomeBase last reported. eufy's device list does not pair it to this HomeBase, or names no slot for it. If the device was removed or re-paired, reload the integration; otherwise check that it is still paired in the eufy app.

setting_mode_table_refused.message: The HomeBase's table for this guard mode cannot be written back unchanged, so nothing was sent and {target} still shows the value the HomeBase last reported. A paired device does not report its settings for the mode, a device is of a kind this integration cannot keep unchanged, or devices hold different delays for the mode. Check the mode's settings in the eufy app.

setting_unconfirmed.message: The device did not confirm the change to {target} in time. It may still apply: the entity shows unknown until the next update shows the value in force.

setting_value_invalid.message: {target} does not accept this value, so nothing was sent. Choose a value the setting allows: a number must sit on one of its steps from the minimum, as the slider offers.

station_unreachable.message: The HomeBase did not answer, so {target} was not set. Home Assistant keeps reconnecting; check that the HomeBase is powered on and on this network.

on_demand_unreachable.message: The camera did not answer, so {target} was not set. A battery camera sleeps between commands and takes about ten seconds to wake; check that it is charged and within Wi-Fi range, then try again.

session_replaced_see_repairs.message: Another app or device signed in with the eufy account and ended Home Assistant's session, so {target} was not set. Waking a battery camera needs a key from eufy, which refuses the ended session. Open the account's repair under Settings > System > Repairs to sign in again, or use Reconfigure on the account entry; Home Assistant does not sign in again by itself.

station_key_rejected.message: The station rejected its key, so {target} was not set. Open its repair under Settings > System > Repairs to let Home Assistant fetch its key once more.

station_key_unusable.message: eufy serves this station a key that cannot be used, so {target} was not set. See its repair under Settings > System > Repairs.

cloud_unavailable.message: Changing {target} needed the HomeBase's key fetched from eufy again, and eufy could not be reached or is temporarily refusing this account, so it was not set. Check Settings > System > Repairs for this account and try again later; Home Assistant does not sign in again by itself.

cache_unavailable.message: The eufy account's cached device list is not available, and eufy cannot be reached right now. Home Assistant retries setting it up.

device_list_refresh_failed.message: The device list could not be fetched from eufy, so nothing changed. Check Settings > System > Repairs for this account and try again later.

capture_in_progress.message: The camera is busy taking another image, so nothing was sent. A capture takes about ten seconds; try again after it.

preset_not_set.message: Preset {index} is not set on this camera, so nothing was sent. Set it in the eufy app, then press Refresh presets.

presets_unsupported.message: This camera has no pan/tilt presets, so nothing was sent.

default_preset_needs_confirmation.message: The camera asks to confirm before making this preset its default, so nothing was changed. Choose the default preset in the eufy app, then press Refresh presets.

pan_tilt_not_applied.message: The camera did not take the pan/tilt step, so it did not move. It may still be turning from the last command; wait a few seconds and try again.

pan_tilt_unsupported.message: This camera cannot pan, tilt or zoom, so nothing was sent.

zoom_unsupported.message: This camera has no zoom, so nothing was sent.

ptz_command_not_handled.message: The HomeBase refused this camera command as one it does not handle, so the camera did not change. Trying again will not help.

zoom_needs_single_view.message: The camera zooms only in single view, so nothing was sent. Switch it to single view in the eufy app, then try again.

presets_full.message: All {slots} preset slots are in use; delete a preset first. Nothing was saved.

preset_not_saved.message: The camera did not save the view as a preset. It may still be turning from the last command; wait a few seconds and try again.

preset_saved_not_default.message: The view was saved as a preset, but the camera did not make it its default. Choose it in Default preset to try again.

preset_not_deleted.message: The camera still holds preset {index}, so it was not deleted. Wait a few seconds and try again.

preset_slot_unknown.message: This camera has no preset slot {index}, so nothing was sent.

recording_in_progress.message: This camera is already recording a clip, so no second one was started. Wait for the running clip to finish, then try again.

recording_needs_history.message: Clips are saved in the event history, which is off. Set Event history to 1 day or more in the integration's options, then try again.

recording_unsupported.message: This camera has no live stream in Home Assistant, so it cannot record a clip.

live_stream_limit.message: The HomeBase has no session free for another live stream: the sessions per HomeBase option allows {limit} at once and none ended in time. Close another live view of this HomeBase, or raise the option, then try again.

camera_unavailable.message: The camera sent no picture, so no clip was saved. A battery camera sleeps between uses and takes a few seconds to wake; check that it is charged and within Wi-Fi range, then try again.

recording_failed.message: The camera sent the clip, but Home Assistant could not save it to the event history. Check that the media folder is writable and has free space, and that Home Assistant's ffmpeg works; the log has the details.

capture_preset.name: Capture preset image
capture_preset.description: Turns a pan/tilt camera to one of its preset positions and takes a live image of that view, shown by that preset's image entity. Wakes a battery camera and leaves it at the preset.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: The preset slot's index as the camera reports it; the first slot is 0.

pan_tilt.name: Pan or tilt
pan_tilt.description: Moves a pan/tilt camera one fixed step, as its Pan and Tilt buttons do. Wakes a battery camera; it returns to its default preset once idle.

goto_preset.name: Go to preset
goto_preset.description: Turns a pan/tilt camera to one of its preset positions once, without taking an image. Wakes a battery camera; it returns to its default preset once idle. The live view preset is not changed.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: The preset slot's index as the camera reports it; the first slot is 0.

zoom.name: Zoom
zoom.description: Zooms the live view one step in or out, as the Live view zoom slider does. With a live view open the camera zooms at once; otherwise the next live view opens at that zoom.

save_preset.name: Save preset
save_preset.description: Stores what a pan/tilt camera shows now as a preset: in its lowest free slot, or over the given one. Use it while the live view runs, or within a few seconds of the last pan or tilt: the camera returns to its default view a few seconds after the last move. Returns the slot index when a response is asked for.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: Overwrite this slot instead of taking the lowest free one; the first slot is 0.

make_default.name: Make default
make_default.description: Also make the saved preset the one the camera returns to when idle; the camera turns there.

delete_preset.name: Delete preset
delete_preset.description: Clears one preset slot of a pan/tilt camera. Its entities go unavailable; deleting the default preset leaves the camera without one until another is chosen.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: The preset slot's index as the camera reports it; the first slot is 0.

record.name: Record clip
record.description: Records a clip of the camera's live stream and saves it as an MP4 in the event history, next to the camera's images. Wakes a battery camera for the clip's length. Shares a running live view instead of opening a second stream. Returns the saved file's media id, its length and whether it is complete when a response is asked for.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Seconds to record, from 5 to 300. Without it, the Recording length option is used.
